text: function explains group's wagebill changes one period next, decomposing change effect due headcount, effect due average pay, effect due moving together. 1. Building panel. Rows missing value measure_col group_cols dropped. group \(g\) (combination group_cols) period \(t\) (ref_date): headcount \(N_{g,t}\): number records; wage \(C_{g,t}\): mean measure_col; wagebill \(W_{g,t} = \sum_i w_i = N_{g,t} \, C_{g,t}\). Every group expanded every ref_date data. group absent period gets \(N = 0\), \(W = 0\) \(C\) = NA, gaps explicit rather silently skipped. Reference dates absent whole data added. row compared group's previous reference date, \(t-1\). 2. Continuing groups (observed \(t-1\) \(t\)). Write \(\Delta N = N_t - N_{t-1}\) \(\Delta C = C_t - C_{t-1}\) (delta_wage). Since \(W_t = (N_{t-1} + \Delta N)(C_{t-1} + \Delta C)\), expanding product gives us following identity: $$W_t - W_{t-1} = \underbrace{C_{t-1} \Delta N}_{\text{employment}} +   \underbrace{N_{t-1} \Delta C}_{\text{wage}} +   \underbrace{\Delta N \, \Delta C}_{\text{interaction}}$$ employment_effect \(= C_{t-1} \Delta N\): change pay stayed last period's average headcount changed. wage_effect \(= N_{t-1} \Delta C\): change headcount stayed last period's level average pay changed. interaction_effect \(= \Delta N \, \Delta C\): extra change moving (new staff paid new average). 3. Entry exit. group missing one two periods, \(\Delta C\) undefined, three effects NA entire change attributed entry exit: entry (absent \(t-1\), present \(t\)): entry_effect \(= W_t\). exit (present \(t-1\), absent \(t\)): exit_effect \(= -W_{t-1}\). Later periods group stays absent also labelled "exit" carry exit_effect = 0, nothing changed. group absent panel's first period likewise "exit" 0 enters. group disappears later reappears therefore shows one exit, zero-effect "exit" rows gap, one entry. 4. Total effect. total_effect sum effects apply row, always equals \(W_t - W_{t-1}\) (\(W = 0\) unobserved). NA panel's first period ("start"), baseline. Consequently, summing total_effect time group recovers wagebill last period minus wagebill first period.

Decomposition. Following Foster, Haltiwanger Krizan (2001), \(\Delta\) change \(t-1\) \(t\): $$\Delta \bar{C}_t =   \underbrace{\sum_{g \K} s_{g,t-1} \Delta C_g}_{\text{within}} +   \underbrace{\sum_{g \K} \Delta s_g (C_{g,t-1} - \bar{C}_{t-1})}_{\text{}} +   \underbrace{\sum_{g \K} \Delta s_g \, \Delta C_g}_{\text{cross}} +   \underbrace{\sum_{g \E} s_{g,t} (C_{g,t} - \bar{C}_{t-1})}_{\text{entry}} -   \underbrace{\sum_{g \X} s_{g,t-1} (C_{g,t-1} - \bar{C}_{t-1})}_{\text{exit}}$$ Within (\(\sum_K s_{g,t-1} \Delta C_g\)): pay growth inside continuing groups, weighted previous-period headcount shares. Pure pay effect. (\(\sum_K \Delta s_g (C_{g,t-1} - \bar{C}_{t-1})\)): movement headcount toward groups paid previous period's overall average (positive) (negative), previous-period pay. Pure composition effect. Cross (\(\sum_K \Delta s_g \, \Delta C_g\)): positive groups gaining headcount share also ones whose pay grows fastest. Entry (\(\sum_E s_{g,t} (C_{g,t} - \bar{C}_{t-1})\)): new groups raise average pay previous period's overall average. Exit (\(-\sum_X s_{g,t-1} (C_{g,t-1} - \bar{C}_{t-1})\)): departing groups raise average paid less previous period's overall average. Proof identity. Shares sum one period, subtracting previous period's average wage every group average leaves change unaltered: $$\Delta \bar{C}_t = \sum_{g \K \cup E} s_{g,t} (C_{g,t} - \bar{C}_{t-1}) -   \sum_{g \K \cup X} s_{g,t-1} (C_{g,t-1} - \bar{C}_{t-1})$$ Substituting \(s_{g,t} = s_{g,t-1} + \Delta s_g\) \(C_{g,t} = C_{g,t-1} + \Delta C_g\) continuing groups yields within, cross terms; entry exit terms remain. Given raw (age, rate) observations one specific outcome curve (e.g. "male pensioner rate age"), returns smoothed rate every age full_ages – including ages zero raw observations . method used depends much data actually available, since local regression needs enough support stable: Exactly one distinct age observed: trend fit single point, one rate repeated flat across whole grid.
